accuracy.evidence: Checked against NC Year 3 multiplication and division (two-digit × one-digit with known tables, mental progressing to formal written methods) and the topic evidence (23 × 4 by partitioning, 96 ÷ 8 with table facts, short multiplication layout). Hand-checked every figure: 23 × 4 = 92, 47 × 3 = 141, 34 × 5 = 170, 46 × 3 = 138, 96 ÷ 8 = 12, 68 ÷ 4 = 17, 84 ÷ 4 = 21, 75 ÷ 5 = 15; parameterised answers evaluated at range corners by the items gate.

misconceptions.evidence: Names and targets the known slips for this stage: multiplying only the tens (83), dropping the carried ten (82, 121), concatenating partial products (812, 1221), digit-by-digit division (9 ÷ 8 and 6 ÷ 8), stopping after the first chunk (96 ÷ 8 = 10), and reporting what is left instead of the group count.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagwmd combines a draggable tens/ones cut through a 23-by-4 array, a carry tile dragged into a column layout, a three-way worked-slip pick, and a division bar filled with dragged fact chunks plus an inverse check; the times-table labs (flagttfam, flagttdbl, flagtt12) only drill recall and flagcommul only turns arrays. Lab gate shingle overlap under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Moving the cut shows the two partial products and their sum live, so the learner finds that cutting at 20 makes both facts easy; dropping the 12 in the ones column is refused with 'only one digit fits'; over-large chunks are refused with the amount left, so the group count emerges from the bar.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions each carry a tempting slip the lab then disproves: '83 (20 × 4, then add 3)' and '812' for 23 × 4, 'next to the 2 in the ones' for the carry, '11 (9 ÷ 8 and 6 ÷ 8)' and '10' for 96 ÷ 8, and '8' or '18' for what is left of 68.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with wrong answers built from the slips and tagged ones, carry, join, rem, sub and mult; each tag has its own message naming the slip (for example 'You lost the carried ten', 'You stopped after the first chunk').

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and the Year 3 terms split, tens, ones, carry, groups, check; family kid FK within the 5.0 target in validate_lessons; adult text names the programme of study, the distributive law, chunking and six mistakes.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate clean; every kid paragraph is one worked step (partition, ones and carry, tens, chunk and check) and each lab step adds one new idea with its own numbers.

mobile.evidence: At 390 px the 23-column array keeps 15 px cells and a 10 px cut handle with a full-height drag zone; column digits are 28 px; chunk chips and fact rows are large tap targets; young-mode buttons 56 px; screenshots checked on iPhone 13 in both themes.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin (Move cut left/right, 1 ten to tens, + chunk buttons, answer and fact buttons); the canvas aria-label is rewritten with each result; walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes.

sources: Department for Education, National Curriculum in England: mathematics programmes of study, Year 3 multiplication and division: write and calculate mathematical statements for multiplication and division using the multiplication tables that they know, including for two-digit numbers times one-digit numbers, using mental and progressing to formal written methods
